title: Julius Caesar crosses the Rubicon
summary: Julius Caesar led a legion across the Rubicon river into Italy proper, defying the Senate's order to disband his army. He is said to have declared that the die was cast.
reason: The Senate, led by Caesar's rivals around Pompey, demanded that he give up his command, which would have exposed him to prosecution.
significance: It began the civil war that ended the Roman Republic, and the phrase became a byword for a point of no return.

title: The Vandals capture Carthage
summary: Genseric's Vandals seized Carthage by surprise, breaking a treaty with Rome, and made it the capital of their kingdom.
reason: The Vandals sought the rich grain lands of Africa Proconsularis, the bread basket of Rome.
significance: Losing Africa's grain and taxes was a heavy blow to the Western Roman Empire.

title: Caliph al-Mansur founds Baghdad
summary: The Abbasid caliph al-Mansur laid the foundations of a new capital, the round city of Baghdad, on the Tigris. It was planned as a circle with the palace and mosque at its centre.
reason: The Abbasids wanted a capital away from Umayyad Syria, near their supporters in Iraq and Persia and on major trade routes.
significance: Baghdad became the largest city of its age and the centre of the Islamic Golden Age.

title: Fourth Crusade sacks Constantinople
summary: Crusaders and Venetians stormed Constantinople and plundered the city for three days, then set up a Latin Empire in its place.
reason: The crusaders were deep in debt to Venice and had been drawn into a Byzantine succession dispute that broke down into war.
significance: It shattered the Byzantine Empire and deepened the hostility between Catholic and Orthodox Christians.

title: Tran Hung Dao defeats the Yuan fleet at Bach Dang
summary: Vietnamese forces led by Tran Hung Dao trapped the Yuan fleet on iron-tipped stakes driven into the bed of the Bach Dang River at low tide and destroyed it.
reason: Kublai Khan had sent a third invasion to conquer Dai Viet after earlier failures.
significance: It ended Mongol attempts to conquer Vietnam and made Tran Hung Dao a national hero.
place: Bach Dang River, Quang Ninh, Vietnam

title: Michelangelo's David is unveiled in Florence
summary: Michelangelo's five-metre marble statue of the biblical David was unveiled outside the Palazzo Vecchio in Florence.
reason: The cathedral works had commissioned the statue, and the city chose a public site where it could stand for the defiant Florentine republic.
significance: It became the defining masterpiece of High Renaissance sculpture.

title: The image of Our Lady of Guadalupe appears to Juan Diego
summary: According to tradition, the Virgin Mary appeared to the indigenous convert Juan Diego on the hill of Tepeyac, and her image was found imprinted on his cloak.
reason: The account arose in the decade after the Spanish conquest, when friars were seeking to convert the indigenous people of Mexico.
significance: Guadalupe became the most important religious and national symbol of Mexico and a major Catholic pilgrimage site.
place: Hill of Tepeyac, Mexico City, Mexico

title: English fleet scatters the Spanish Armada at Gravelines
summary: After fireships broke up the Armada's formation off Calais, English ships attacked it off Gravelines. Winds then drove the Spanish fleet into the North Sea.
reason: Philip II sent the Armada to escort an army from the Netherlands to invade England and end English support for the Dutch revolt.
significance: The failure of the invasion secured Protestant England and its rise as a naval power.

title: The Gunpowder Plot is foiled in London
summary: Guy Fawkes was arrested guarding barrels of gunpowder in a cellar beneath the House of Lords, ending a plot to blow up Parliament and King James I.
reason: A group of English Catholics led by Robert Catesby hoped to kill the Protestant king and restore a Catholic monarchy.
significance: Its failure is still marked each year on Bonfire Night and hardened anti-Catholic laws in England.
place: Palace of Westminster, London, United Kingdom

title: Cossacks swear allegiance to the Tsar at Pereiaslav
summary: A Cossack council led by Hetman Bohdan Khmelnytsky agreed at Pereiaslav to place the Cossack Hetmanate under the protection of the Russian tsar.
reason: The Cossacks, in revolt against Poland-Lithuania since 1648, needed a strong ally to survive.
significance: It brought much of Ukraine under Russian rule and remains contested in Ukrainian and Russian memory.

title: An earthquake sinks much of Port Royal, Jamaica
summary: A strong earthquake liquefied the sandy spit on which Port Royal stood, and much of the city slid into the sea, followed by a tsunami.
reason: Port Royal was built on loose sand and gravel, which turned to liquid when the ground shook.
significance: About 2,000 people died at once and the richest port of the English Caribbean was ruined.

title: Bach's St Matthew Passion is first performed
summary: Johann Sebastian Bach's St Matthew Passion, for two choirs and two orchestras, was performed at the Good Friday vespers in Leipzig's St. Thomas Church.
reason: As cantor of St. Thomas, Bach had to supply music for the Lutheran liturgy, including a passion for Good Friday.
significance: It is one of the summits of Western sacred music.

title: Treaty of Allahabad grants the Diwani of Bengal
summary: Mughal emperor Shah Alam II granted the East India Company the right to collect revenue in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.
reason: After defeat at Buxar, the emperor needed Company protection, and Robert Clive wanted a legal basis for Company rule.
significance: It turned a trading company into a territorial power in India.

title: Rama I founds the Chakri dynasty of Siam
summary: General Chao Phraya Chakri took the throne of Siam as King Rama I, and soon moved the capital across the river to Bangkok.
reason: King Taksin had been deposed amid unrest, and the leading general was invited to rule.
significance: The Chakri dynasty still reigns in Thailand.

title: Ranjit Singh captures Lahore
summary: The young Sikh chief Ranjit Singh took Lahore, which became the capital of his rising state.
reason: He was uniting the rival Sikh misls of the Punjab under his rule.
significance: It laid the foundation of the Sikh Empire.

title: Kandyan Convention ends the Kingdom of Kandy
summary: Kandyan chiefs and the British signed an agreement placing the Kandyan Kingdom under the British Crown.
reason: The chiefs had turned against their king, and the British had occupied Kandy.
significance: It brought all of Sri Lanka under British rule.

title: Britain abolishes slavery across most of its empire
summary: The Slavery Abolition Act received royal assent, freeing enslaved people in most British colonies from 1834, with compensation paid to slave owners.
reason: Decades of abolitionist campaigning, slave rebellions such as the Baptist War in Jamaica, and the reformed Parliament made abolition politically possible.
significance: It freed about 800,000 people and made Britain a leading force against slavery worldwide.
place: Palace of Westminster, London, United Kingdom

title: Convention of Peking ends the Second Opium War
summary: After British and French troops occupied Beijing and burned the Old Summer Palace, the Qing signed conventions ceding Kowloon to Britain and opening Tianjin to trade.
reason: The Qing had refused to ratify the 1858 Treaties of Tianjin, and the Western powers marched on the capital to enforce them.
significance: It deepened China's subordination to foreign powers and helped Russia gain the Pacific coast north of Korea.

title: Canadian Confederation creates the Dominion of Canada
summary: The British North America Act came into force, uniting Ontario, Quebec, Nova Scotia and New Brunswick into the Dominion of Canada.
reason: The colonies wanted security against the United States after its Civil War, a common market and a way out of political deadlock in the Province of Canada.
significance: It founded the modern Canadian state.

title: Krakatoa erupts catastrophically
summary: A series of colossal explosions destroyed most of the volcanic island of Krakatoa, and tsunamis swept the coasts of Java and Sumatra, killing more than 36,000 people.
reason: Months of rising activity in the volcano culminated in the collapse of its magma chamber.
significance: The blast was heard thousands of kilometers away and its ash cooled the global climate for years.

title: Mount Pelee erupts and destroys Saint-Pierre
summary: A pyroclastic flow from Mount Pelee on Martinique swept over the town of Saint-Pierre, killing about 28,000 people within minutes; only a handful survived.
reason: The volcano had shown warning signs for weeks, but authorities kept residents in town, partly because of an upcoming election.
significance: It was the deadliest volcanic eruption of the twentieth century and transformed the study of volcanic hazards.

title: Louis Bleriot flies across the English Channel
summary: French aviator Louis Bleriot flew his Bleriot XI monoplane from near Calais to Dover in about 37 minutes, the first flight across a large body of water in a heavier-than-air aircraft.
reason: The Daily Mail newspaper offered a prize for the first flight across the Channel.
significance: It showed that Britain was no longer protected by the sea and boosted public faith in aviation.

title: Austria-Hungary declares war on Serbia
summary: Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia by telegram, and alliance commitments drew Russia, Germany, France and Britain into war within a week.
reason: Vienna blamed Serbia for the Sarajevo assassination and, backed by Germany, issued an ultimatum it expected Serbia to reject.
significance: It began World War I, which killed millions and remade the world order.

title: Sharif Hussein launches the Arab Revolt
summary: Sharif Hussein bin Ali of Mecca proclaimed a revolt against Ottoman rule, and his forces attacked the Ottoman garrison in Mecca.
reason: Hussein sought an independent Arab state and had British promises of support in the Hussein-McMahon correspondence.
significance: The revolt helped end Ottoman rule in the Arab lands and launched modern Arab nationalism.

title: Alexander Fleming discovers penicillin
summary: At St Mary's Hospital in London, Alexander Fleming noticed that a mold contaminating a culture plate had killed the surrounding Staphylococcus bacteria.
reason: Fleming was studying bacteria and, returning from holiday, examined plates left out during his absence.
significance: Penicillin, developed into a drug in the 1940s, began the age of antibiotics and saved countless lives.
place: St Mary's Hospital, Paddington, London, United Kingdom

title: Italy invades Ethiopia
summary: Italian troops crossed from Eritrea into Ethiopia without a declaration of war, beginning the Second Italo-Ethiopian War.
reason: Mussolini sought an empire and revenge for Italy's defeat at Adwa in 1896.
significance: The League of Nations' failure to stop the invasion discredited collective security.

title: Hahn and Strassmann discover nuclear fission
summary: In Berlin, Otto Hahn and Fritz Strassmann detected barium after bombarding uranium with neutrons, which Lise Meitner and Otto Frisch soon explained as the splitting of the nucleus.
reason: Physicists across Europe were studying what happened when uranium was bombarded with neutrons.
significance: It opened the way to nuclear power and the atomic bomb.
place: Kaiser Wilhelm Institute for Chemistry, Berlin, Germany

title: Earthquake devastates Erzincan in eastern Turkey
summary: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake on the North Anatolian Fault destroyed the city of Erzincan in the middle of a winter night. About 33,000 people died, many from the cold after their homes collapsed.
reason: The North Anatolian Fault is one of the most active faults in the world, where the Anatolian Plate slides past the Eurasian Plate.
significance: It was the deadliest earthquake in modern Turkish history until 1999 and began a series of large ruptures along the fault.

title: Penicillin is first given to a patient in Oxford
summary: At the Radcliffe Infirmary, police constable Albert Alexander, dying of a severe infection, became the first patient treated with purified penicillin. He improved dramatically, but supplies ran out and he died weeks later.
reason: Howard Florey and Ernst Chain's team had turned Alexander Fleming's 1928 discovery into a usable drug, but could make only tiny amounts.
significance: It showed penicillin worked in people and led to the mass production that saved countless lives by the war's end.

title: Battle of Midway turns the tide in the Pacific
summary: US carrier aircraft sank four Japanese fleet carriers near Midway Atoll, losing only one of their own.
reason: Japan planned to lure the remaining US carriers into a trap, but American codebreakers had read its plans.
significance: It destroyed the core of Japan's carrier force and shifted the initiative in the Pacific to the United States.

title: Avery, MacLeod and McCarty show DNA carries genes
summary: Oswald Avery, Colin MacLeod and Maclyn McCarty published evidence that DNA, not protein, was the substance that could transform harmless bacteria into deadly ones.
reason: They were trying to identify the 'transforming principle' that Frederick Griffith had found in pneumococcus bacteria in 1928.
significance: It was the first strong proof that genes are made of DNA, opening the way to modern molecular biology.
place: Rockefeller Institute, New York City, United States

title: George Marshall proposes the Marshall Plan
summary: In a speech at Harvard University, Secretary of State George Marshall proposed large scale American aid to rebuild Europe.
reason: Europe was struggling with hunger and ruined economies, and Washington feared that poverty would help communist parties.
significance: The plan financed Western Europe's recovery and deepened the split with the Soviet bloc.
place: Harvard University, Cambridge, Massachusetts, United States

title: Joseph Stalin dies
summary: Soviet leader Joseph Stalin died at his dacha at Kuntsevo near Moscow, days after a stroke.
reason: Stalin was 74 and had been in failing health.
significance: His death opened a power struggle and a gradual thaw in the Soviet Union.
wikipedia: Death and state funeral of Joseph Stalin

title: Jack Kilby demonstrates the first integrated circuit
summary: At Texas Instruments in Dallas, Jack Kilby demonstrated a working circuit built on a single piece of germanium.
reason: Engineers were looking for a way around the tangle of wires needed to connect many separate components.
significance: The integrated circuit made microchips and modern computing possible.
place: Texas Instruments, Dallas, Texas, United States

title: The Beatles appear on The Ed Sullivan Show
summary: The Beatles performed live on The Ed Sullivan Show in New York, watched by about 73 million Americans.
reason: Their records had just topped the American charts, and the visit was heavily promoted.
significance: It launched the British Invasion of American pop music.
place: Ed Sullivan Theater, New York City, United States
wikipedia: The Beatles in the United States

title: Apollo 11 lands on the Moon
summary: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin landed the lunar module Eagle on the Sea of Tranquility, and Armstrong became the first person to walk on the Moon.
reason: President Kennedy had set the goal of a Moon landing within the decade, in the space race with the Soviet Union.
significance: It was the first time humans set foot on another world.

title: Arab oil producers announce an oil embargo
summary: Arab members of OPEC meeting in Kuwait decided to cut oil production, followed by an embargo on the United States and other supporters of Israel.
reason: They wanted to punish Western support for Israel in the Yom Kippur War.
significance: Oil prices quadrupled, causing recession and changing energy policy worldwide.
participants: Organization of Arab Petroleum Exporting Countries

title: The WHO declares smallpox eradicated
summary: The World Health Assembly in Geneva declared that smallpox had been eradicated, the first human disease wiped out.
reason: A global vaccination and surveillance campaign since 1967 had tracked down the last cases.
significance: It is one of the greatest achievements of public health.

title: The last Soviet troops leave Afghanistan
summary: General Boris Gromov walked across the Friendship Bridge into Soviet Uzbekistan, the last Soviet soldier to leave Afghanistan.
reason: After a decade of war with mujahideen, Gorbachev decided to withdraw under the Geneva Accords.
significance: It ended a war that drained the Soviet Union and left Afghanistan in civil war.

title: The World Wide Web becomes publicly available
summary: Tim Berners-Lee posted a summary of the World Wide Web project to Usenet, inviting anyone to use it and contribute.
reason: He had built the system at CERN to help physicists share documents across different computers.
significance: The web turned the internet into a mass medium.

title: Dayton Agreement ends the Bosnian War
summary: The leaders of Bosnia, Serbia and Croatia formally signed in Paris the peace deal negotiated in Dayton, Ohio.
reason: NATO bombing and Croatian and Bosniak offensives pushed the Bosnian Serbs to negotiate.
significance: It ended Europe's bloodiest war since 1945 and created Bosnia's current constitution.

title: Angola's civil war ends with a ceasefire
summary: Angola's government and UNITA signed a ceasefire memorandum in Luanda, six weeks after UNITA leader Jonas Savimbi was killed.
reason: Savimbi's death left the rebels leaderless and ready to negotiate.
significance: It ended a 27-year war that had killed hundreds of thousands.

title: Hurricane Katrina hits the US Gulf Coast
summary: Katrina made landfall in Louisiana, and failing levees flooded most of New Orleans. About 1,400 people died.
reason: A strong storm met a city below sea level protected by poorly built levees.
significance: The slow response became a national scandal about poverty and government failure.

title: South Sudan becomes independent
summary: South Sudan declared independence from Sudan in Juba, becoming the world's newest country.
reason: Decades of civil war ended with a 2005 peace deal and a referendum in which almost all voters chose independence.
significance: It split Africa's largest country in two.

title: Military takes control in Zimbabwe, ending Mugabe's rule
summary: Zimbabwe's army seized control of Harare and placed President Robert Mugabe under house arrest. He resigned a week later.
reason: Mugabe had fired his deputy Emmerson Mnangagwa to clear the way for his wife Grace.
significance: It ended 37 years of rule by Mugabe.

title: Chandrayaan-3 lands near the Moon's south pole
summary: India's Chandrayaan-3 lander touched down near the lunar south pole.
reason: India sought to succeed after its 2019 lander crashed and to study ice near the pole.
significance: India became the fourth country to soft-land on the Moon and the first near its south pole.
